sentences.text: Palaeotis weigelti stood slightly under one meter tall.
This flightless bird possessed relatively large wings, indicated by its spindly humerus, unlike modern flightless birds.
Researchers suggest Palaeotis likely had carnivorous habits, suggested by its slender beak similar to lithornithids.
The genus Palaeotis was first described by Lambrecht in 1928.
The holotype of Palaeotis consists of a fossil tarsometatarsus and phalanx.
Houde and Haubold discovered three additional specimens of Palaeotis in the Geiseltalmuseum collection in Germany.
A specimen of Palaeotis cataloged as HLMD Me 7530 was collected from the Messel shales.
Palaeotis is considered to be a flightless bird.
Researchers suggest Palaeotis was sexually dimorphic based on size differences between specimens.
Houde and Haubold reclassified Palaeotis as a palaeognath in the order Struthioniformes, placing it with ostriches, and the species is classified within the family Struthionidae.
The only known species of Palaeotis is P. weigelti.
Palaeotis lived in central Europe during the middle Eocene epoch.
The fossil record of Palaeotis spans from 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.

Some scientists debate the classification of Palaeotis, arguing it is a basal ratite rather than a struthioniform, while others are less convinced it is a struthioniform and instead place it as a more basal ratite.
